name: Zona mista / gioco all'italiana
scopeNote: Zona mista (mixed zone), also 'modulo misto' and in English 'gioco all'italiana': man-marking on the opposing playmaker or striker plus zonal cover, a sweeper, four defenders, results-first and quick transitions. Period anchored on Trapattoni's first Juventus spell (1976-07-01 to 1986-06-30; 1 July/30 June taken from a search summary, not a read page). Spielverlagerung dates the tactic from the second half of the 1970s to the mid-1990s and credits Radice (Torino) and Trapattoni; Wikipedia says it 'combined the strength of zonal marking with that of catenaccio'. Labelling caveat: Trapattoni is often tagged 'catenacciaro'; Il Giornale calls that a propaganda label, and 90min says late-1970s Juve still showed 'remnants of catenaccio'. Distinct from catenaccio (rigid sweeper plus man-marking, double-marking), from Sacchi's pure zonal pressing (which zona mista predates and which is high-line) and from resultadismo (a stance, not a marking scheme). Evidence is mostly tier B-C retrospectives; no read page covers pressing intensity, set pieces or exact line height.
openQuestions: Proposed ids not yet in the catalog: manager 'giovanni-trapattoni' (Juventus 1976-86, 1991-94) and team 'juventus-1976-86'. Existing ids found: only 'juventus-2014-19' (team), 'arrigo-sacchi', 'carlo-ancelotti' (manager). Confirm before creating.

Radice (Torino, scudetto 1975/76) is credited as co-originator by Spielverlagerung and Wikipedia; Wikipedia's Torino-first claim was not independently checked. Proposed exemplar 'luigi-radice' (manager) if wanted.
Trapattoni's own writing (Coaching High Performance Soccer, 2000) is cited in Wikipedia's reference list but was not read; the only Trapattoni defence quote ('difesa mista') is undated on Wikiquote.

Wikipedia's treble/Intercontinental claim ('first club ... European Treble', 1985) was not used as evidence; spells dates 1976-07-01/1986-06-30 come from a search summary and should be checked against a second source.
Italy 1982 (Bearzot) as a national-team exemplar: Wikipedia and TFT say Bearzot also used zona mista; could be added as a team exemplar if the catalog has it.

Distinctness: zona mista overlaps catenaccio (man-marking + libero); the difference sources give is zonal swapping of positions, attacking libero/full-backs and transition speed. Pressing is not evidenced as a feature.

sources.title: Zona Mista (Spielverlagerung glossary)
sources.evidence: Zona Mista, often referred to as Gioco all’italiana, is a tactic used in Italian football mainly since the second half of 1970s to mid-1990s. The introduction of this system has been attributed to Luigi Radice and Giovanni Trapattoni. Zona Mista as a tactical theory evolved the Catenaccio system.

sources.title: Zona Mista (Spielverlagerung glossary)
sources.evidence: A player, who leaves the zone that was initially covered, is replaced by a team-mate, thus retaining the team’s intended organisational structure.
